paper.task: Raw audio X goes in; a convolutional feature encoder gives latent speech representations z, a Transformer context network gives context representations c; the model is pre-trained self-supervised (contrastive task on masked time steps against quantized latents q, plus a diversity loss) and then fine-tuned for speech recognition into C vocabulary classes with a CTC loss.

components.name: raw audio
components.what: raw waveform X, the model input; normalized to zero mean and unit variance before the encoder

provenance.quote: multi-layer convolutional feature encoder f : X 7→ Z which takes as input raw audio X

components.name: feature encoder
components.what: multi-layer convolutional encoder f: X -> Z; several blocks, each a temporal convolution followed by layer normalization and a GELU; its total stride sets the number of time-steps T

provenance.quote: The encoder consists of several blocks containing a temporal convolution followed by layer normalization

components.name: latent speech representations
components.what: feature encoder output z_1, ..., z_T, one vector per time-step

provenance.quote: outputs latent speech representations z 1 , . . . , z T for T time-steps

components.name: masking
components.what: masks a proportion of the feature encoder outputs before the context network: samples a proportion p of time steps as start indices and masks the next M consecutive steps (spans may overlap), replacing them with one trained feature vector shared by all masked steps; pre-training only

provenance.quote: We mask a proportion of the feature encoder outputs, or time steps before feeding them to the context network and replace them with a trained feature vector shared between all masked time steps

components.name: context network
components.what: Transformer g: Z -> C; uses a convolutional layer (followed by a GELU, added to its inputs, then layer normalization) as relative positional embedding instead of fixed positional embeddings

provenance.quote: The output of the feature encoder is fed to a context network which follows the Transformer architecture

components.name: context representations
components.what: context network output c_1, ..., c_T, capturing information from the entire sequence

provenance.quote: a Transformer g : Z 7→ C to build representations c 1 , . . . , c T capturing information from the entire sequence

components.name: quantization module
components.what: product quantization Z -> Q: z is mapped to G x V logits; G hard Gumbel softmax operations (straight-through estimator) pick one entry from each of G codebooks; the G entries are concatenated and linearly transformed (R^d -> R^f) to give q; used for self-supervised training only

provenance.quote: For self-supervised training we discretize the output of the feature encoder z to a finite set of speech representations via product quantization

components.name: quantized latent speech representations
components.what: quantized representations q_t in R^f, the targets of the self-supervised objective

provenance.quote: The output of the feature encoder is discretized to q t with a quantization module Z 7→ Q to represent the targets

components.name: contrastive loss
components.what: L_m: for a masked time step t, identify the true quantized q_t among K+1 candidates (q_t and K distractors sampled from other masked time steps of the same utterance) using cosine similarity with the context output c_t

provenance.quote: we learn representations of speech audio by solving a contrastive task L m which requires to identify the true quantized latent speech representation for a masked time step within a set of distractors

components.name: diversity loss
components.what: L_d: maximizes the entropy of the averaged softmax distribution over each codebook's entries across a batch, so the V entries of the G codebooks are used equally often

provenance.quote: This is augmented by a codebook diversity loss L d to encourage the model to use the codebook entries equally often

components.name: linear projection
components.what: randomly initialized linear projection added on top of the context network for fine-tuning; outputs C classes (for Librispeech 29 character tokens plus a word boundary token)

provenance.quote: Pre-trained models are fine-tuned for speech recognition by adding a randomly initialized linear projection on top of the context network into C classes representing the vocabulary of the task

components.name: CTC loss
components.what: fine-tuning objective minimized for speech recognition

provenance.quote: Models are optimized by minimizing a CTC loss

contributions.text: Compared to vq-wav2vec, the model builds context representations over continuous speech representations, and self-attention captures dependencies over the entire sequence of latent representations end-to-end

provenance.quote: Compared to vq-wav2vec [5], our model builds context representations over continuous speech representations and self-attention captures dependencies over the entire sequence of latent representations end-to-end

unclear: No module is presented as the paper's own design: the feature encoder, Transformer context network, product quantization with Gumbel softmax, BERT-like masking, contrastive loss and diversity loss are all described with citations to prior work. All modules are therefore 'reused' (the weaker role). The only claim of difference is the vq-wav2vec comparison (context built over continuous representations, end-to-end), which concerns how the parts are wired, not one module; it is recorded as a contribution with no components. The orchestrator may decide to mark context_net / quantizer / masking as proposed.
Stage members are exclusive: the feature encoder, latents z, context network and context representations c are used in both pre-training and fine-tuning and are left out of both stage lists.

The text does not say whether masking (Sec. 3.1) is applied during fine-tuning or inference; the main path z -> masking -> context network is recorded with kind 'data'. Where the fine-tuning SpecAugment masking is applied (waveform, latents z, or elsewhere) is not stated, so it is not drawn as a component.

The fine-tuning flows are partly implicit: the text says a linear projection into C classes is added on top of the context network and that models minimize a CTC loss, but it does not explicitly say the CTC loss is computed on the projection outputs, nor how the labeled data / character targets enter it. linear_proj -> ctc_loss is recorded; labeled data is not drawn as a component.

The masked time-step indices decide where L_m is computed (c_t over a masked step) and where distractors are drawn from (other masked steps of the same utterance); the text states no explicit flow from masking to the loss, so none is recorded.

The diversity loss uses the softmax distribution over codebook entries computed inside the quantization module (without Gumbel noise or temperature); it is recorded as a flow quantizer -> l_d. The extracted sentence reads 'averaged softmax distribution l over the codebook entries', with a stray 'l', possibly the logits symbol.
Counts not given in this text: number of feature-encoder blocks ('several'), number of Transformer layers, G, V, K, p, M; kernel sizes and strides are deferred to Sec. 4.2.

Context-network internals (the convolutional relative positional embedding, GELU, residual add to the inputs, layer normalization) are described but not expanded at overview depth because the context network is a reused module; the text does not say exactly which 'inputs' the convolution output is added to (presumably the context network inputs).
Equations (1), (3) and (4) are garbled in the extraction (fraction bars and sums split across lines); their content was taken only from the surrounding words.
The text refers to '(Figure 1)', but this is a blind run, so no figure or caption was consulted.
